speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to help me understand this, are you currently breastfeeding or formula-fed, and has the rash appeared suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is a 4-day-old with a rash present for 1 day; given the maternal history of treated gonorrhea, have the lesions primarily appeared on the palms and soles, or are they more widespread? Also, is there any purulent discharge from the umbilical cord or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection.

The presence of pustules with an erythematous base and involvement of the trunk and extremities, while sparing the palms and soles, is highly consistent with disseminated gonococcal infection despite the prior treatment history. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain and culture of skin pustules and maternal/infant Naegleria testing.
